title: Understanding Rust - FileCleaner App
summary: Read one real Rust application end to end: a macOS tool that reclaims duplicate-file space with APFS clones instead of deletions — the clonefile FFI call, the candidate funnel, and a journaled transaction that survives a power cut.

concepts.title: A Tool That Deletes Nothing
concepts.brief: The problem, the promise, the four CLI commands, the lib/bin split, Cargo.toml and the module tree. Orientation before any code is read closely.

concepts.title: APFS Clones, and Calling clonefile from Rust
concepts.brief: Copy-on-write clones; clone vs hard link vs symlink; the 29-line libc::clonefile wrapper — CString, unsafe, errno, CLONE_NOFOLLOW, EEXIST; why same-volume only; why du still shows full size.

concepts.title: The Domain, Written as Types
concepts.brief: model.rs and policy.rs: newtypes, FileEntry, DuplicateGroup, eligible_targets, logical vs estimated bytes, deterministic source selection by tuple comparison.

concepts.title: Walking the Disk
concepts.brief: scanner/walker.rs and filter.rs: walkdir, filter_entry and the Cell counter, the classification ladder, HashSet dedupe, MetadataExt, into_path as a move.

concepts.title: The Index That Remembers
concepts.brief: index/db.rs: rusqlite bundled, the four tables, WAL, prepared statements in a transaction, query_map error handling, migrate(), &self vs &mut self as a compile-time guarantee, a Rust 2024 let-chain.

concepts.title: The Candidate Funnel
concepts.brief: Size buckets in SQL, a 192 KiB BLAKE3 sample, a streaming SHA-256, then grouping — and why none of it is the final authority. Staleness as a value, rayon for bounded parallelism, resumability.

concepts.title: Errors: anyhow at the Edges, thiserror in the Core
concepts.brief: The three thiserror enums, #[from] and #[error(transparent)], Context on Result and Option, type aliases, and why the split matters for what the CLI can tell the user.

concepts.title: A Seam for Failure: the ApfsAdapter Trait
concepts.brief: One trait, seven methods, all the unsafe behind it; &dyn dispatch; the FaultyAdapter that fails at any chosen step, and the single assertion every fault must satisfy.

concepts.title: Preflight: Earning the Right to Touch a File
concepts.brief: make_plan and the hidden sibling paths; ExpectedTarget; the ten read-only checks in order and why each exists; access(2); why the dry run is exactly this and nothing more.

concepts.title: The Journaled Transaction
concepts.brief: The full sequence: snapshot, byte-compare both forks, clone to temp, restore metadata, verify, journal-before-rename, the post-rename race check, fsync, final validation, backup removal — plus Progress-directed rollback.

concepts.title: Metadata Fidelity
concepts.brief: Why a clone arrives wearing the source's metadata; MetadataSnapshot and RestoreOutcome; the restore order and its reasons; hand-bound ACL and setattrlist FFI; xattr size-then-read with an ERANGE retry.

concepts.title: Crash Recovery, and What We Gained
concepts.brief: TxnState as an enum-shaped state machine, can_transition, roll back before the swap point and roll forward after it, the lost-clone fallback, idempotence — and a closing reflection on the whole design.

notes: Seed brief from the issue form: "The idea of this book is to understand Rust. We are going to take an example application that I have implemented. Its called FileCleaner. A duplicate-file space reclaimer for macOS/APFS. It finds files with byte-identical content and — instead of deleting anything — replaces each duplicate with an APFS clone of a chosen source file. Every file keeps its path, its metadata, and its independence; the data blocks are shared on disk (copy-on-write) until a file is modified. I want you to get the source code of this application from here, https://github.com/sunprema/file_cleaner . It has Rust and a SwiftApp. The focus for this book is only the Rust application. You should explain how this application is implemented, the libraries used. Basically this is an application that a developer that know just the basics of Rust can learn from. You should also explain the ADFS Clone mechanism as well." Source repository read in full for this build (~3,600 lines of Rust, edition 2024, bin `filecleaner` + lib `file_cleaner`); every code listing is real code from that repo. Ignore FileCleanerApp/ (SwiftUI) except to note that a native UI drives the same engine.
